name: Il Borro
insider_take: This medieval borgo turned luxury resort sits on a 1,700-acre estate where Ferragamo family heritage meets Tuscan authenticity in the most enchanting way possible.
whats_special: Il Borro is actually a restored 14th-century village owned by the Ferragamo family, featuring original stone buildings that once housed an entire medieval community. The estate produces its own award-winning wines, olive oil, and even has a working farm where guests can participate in harvest activities. The property's chapel still hosts real weddings, and many of the suites are housed in buildings that were once village shops and homes.
pro_tip: Book the exclusive "Master's Table" experience where you'll dine in Salvatore Ferragamo's private study, surrounded by his personal collection of shoes and fashion sketches.
dont_miss: The estate's incredible truffle hunting experiences with trained dogs during season (October-December), and a visit to the on-site artisan workshops where local craftsmen still practice traditional Tuscan trades like pottery and leather working. The property's infinity pool offers breathtaking views over the Arno Valley that inspired Renaissance masters.
pros: Historic borgo estate with medieval charm and authentic Tuscan architecture
Award-winning organic wine estate with on-site vineyard tours and tastings
Michelin-starred dining featuring farm-to-table cuisine with estate-grown ingredients
Luxurious spa treatments using organic products from the estate's gardens
cons: Remote countryside location requires car rental for exploring beyond the estate
Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive Relais & Châteaux positioning
